symptom: `mxcli test` stops at injection with `Parse error: line 8:75 mismatched input 'ON' expecting ';'` (and a misleading `'Error' is a keyword` hint) when a test body's call has its own `on error rollback` / `on error continue` / custom handler — no test runs
cause: `attachOnError` appended the runner's `ON ERROR BEGIN … END ERROR` to every line `startsErrorRaisingCall` matched, unconditionally, so a call with its own clause got a second one. The line-based join also broke on a custom handler (its body's first `;` ended the 'statement') and on a trailing `-- comment`. Both runners had their own copy of the join
insight: Find statements by PARSING the body (in the generator's own wrapper and language version) and read each call's own onErrorClause from the tree: a regex cannot tell a clause on the next line from `on error` in a string, a comment or a nested handler. Decide per clause from what Mendix stores: `on error rollback` is the default spelled out (same ErrorHandlingType as no clause), so it gets the runner's handler — keeping it made the same exception an ERROR, failed a matching @throws, and aborted the legacy suite; continue/custom are kept verbatim. Keeping a custom handler opened a FALSE GREEN only a runtime run showed: a handler that ends normally rejoins PAST every statement reading the failed call's output (the flow builder's skip-var rule), i.e. past the @expect checks, and the test returned PASS with nothing evaluated. Fixed fail-closed: each assertion counts itself in both branches and a guard after the last fails a short count — an assertion on what the handler set still passes. The legacy log parser had the twin: a RUN line with no verdict read as PASS (StatusPass is the zero value); a re-raising handler did exactly that. Measured verdict table on 11.13.0 in mdl-examples/bug-tests/test-runner-1448-own-error-handler.test.mdl
